for.platform_descriptor: tests/deterministic/fixtures/isolated-fixture-program-pins.financials-descriptor.json (vacilando.isolated_fixture_program_descriptor.v1, read 2026-10-31 from the platform worktree; uncommitted there, not installed)

installed_contract_today: toolkit 20261031-eeaa6dac6860 registers both Financials entries authority v1; v2 pins require pins.sql. This product child refuses v1 (fixture_authority_org_unbound), so every Financials execution refuses until the platform installs the program variant and these pins.

candidate.candidate_sha: THE COMMIT THAT ADDS THIS FILE (a documentation-only child of the code commit; named in the lane's run report). Every artifact below is byte-identical at both. Any later product commit is a new candidate: re-measure, never reuse.

shared_verifier.provenance: byte-identical from Enrollment commit 80eb7446656f89f0c43da01105836e4d1c64aa56 (not on origin/staging)

product_supplies.artifact_order: as listed (the digest is over the array in this order)

what_the_product_child_checks: authority schema v2 only; a v1 record refuses fixture_authority_org_unbound (no fallback)

shared verifyIsolatedFixtureAuthorityV2: store root from passwd home, record inside <root>/vacilando/isolated-fixture/authority by real path, in-flight request names the file and its sha256, issued_at <= now < expires_at, request/fixture/operation/run/environment/candidate/binding digest = env, program fixture/operation/suite/npm script/script body digest/HEAD = record

fixture_org: isolated = { id 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001, key certification_seed, source seed_manifest }; historical = the org the executor's QA-run ledger binds to the run's persona (OPEN, local, this environment, QA_ORGS key), never the seed org
database_identity: verifyConnectionTarget on DATABASE_URL with the child's whole env as clientEnv (PG* target keys and target-overriding URL parameters refuse; loopback; never 54422; digest equal)
target_hold_disposition: re-read <root>/vacilando/target-holds/<environment>.json; clear, same revision and record_sha256, for this request
API origin: http://127.0.0.1:<port>, never 54421 (shared check), and in the same certenv port block as DATABASE_URL (product guard)

program_pins: re-read from the request-recorded bytes; variant program, no sql, 1-32 unique repository-relative artifacts, digest = sha256(canonicalJson({variant, candidate_sha, script_sha256, artifacts})), candidate_sha = ALLOY_QA_CANDIDATE_SHA = HEAD, script_sha256 = own body, every required artifact present with its role, every artifact's bytes in the checkout = pin
callers (runner, historical entry, vitest guard, live suite) verify FIRST, before binding judgement, credential use, client, import or spawn, and hand clients the verified API origin and org

an artifact absent at the candidate or with other committed bytes
seed program issued a persona org, or historical program issued the seed org

a Financials request ever issued a v1 record after v2 registration

requests_to_the_platform.what: Register both entries authority_contract v2, pins variant 'program', with the artifacts above and candidate_sha = the commit that adds this file.
requests_to_the_platform.why: Without it the product child refuses every execution (by design).

requests_to_the_platform.what: Name the API target in the v2 record: an api_identity { environment_id, host 127.0.0.1, port = the environment's assigned api.port, digest } issued from the environment record, so the child can bind its PostgREST origin exactly, not by port block.
requests_to_the_platform.why: Financials' clients connect through the Supabase API (SUPABASE_URL), not DATABASE_URL. The v2 database identity binds the Postgres target only; the product's same-block guard is a stopgap, not authority.

requests_to_the_platform.what: Keep issuing ALLOY_QA_AUTHORITY_SHA256 and DATABASE_URL to Financials children; keep program_pins inside the authority record (the child re-reads it from the request-recorded bytes).
requests_to_the_platform.why: The child's checks depend on both.

not_claimed: nothing authenticates the issuer cryptographically (same OS user)
pins prove the started bytes, not transitive imports
the API guard is a port-block rule from installed certification-environments.mjs (base 56100, block 10, 20 blocks), not an identity
